abstract: |
  An abstract carrying two marks. [Quoin]{#quoin-passage .index index="gamma"}
  carries an id its author wrote and [Rafter]{.index index="gamma"} carries
  none, and both file the one locator — this chapter's page and no fragment —
  whether this chapter is read from its record or recovered from this source.

# Back matter

Not the last chapter of the book, and carrying no placement marker: it grows no
index section as the fixture stands. It is the chapter a placement marker is
appended to when a check needs a marker to appear between two renders, and the
chapter whose store path a check holds with a directory when it needs a record
that can never be written — both a chapter ahead of the one that reports.

A second term for the index no marker names: [Dovetail]{.index index="gamma"}.

The mark forms below are what makes this chapter's recovery worth fencing: a
chapter read back from its own source has to reach every shape an author
writes, not only the bare mark above. The first group carries no id of its
own, so each of its locators is this chapter's page and nothing after it; the
second group carries ids their authors wrote, which recovery carries into the
locator. Each is on a term no other mark in this
book indexes, because the sort-key registry is keyed on the printed level path
and a term marked in two chapters would put two chapters' keys in question (the
M13 lesson, extended M56).

More than one level, so recovery has to rebuild a sub-entry and the parent it
hangs under: [joinery]{.index entry="Woodwork!Joinery" index="gamma"}.

A declared sort key, which is a value the author wrote rather than a conclusion
this chapter reached, so recovery carries it: [Zephyr]{.index index="gamma"
sort="Abacus"}.

A cross-reference sending the reader somewhere else instead of listing a page,
whose target is a term five.qmd marks: [Ferrule]{.index index="gamma"
see="Escutcheon"}.

A cross-reference sending the reader somewhere else as well — which in this
extension still prints no page of its own: [Hasp]{.index index="gamma"
see-also="Escutcheon"}.

A range that opens [Ingot]{.index index="gamma" range="open"} here and closes
[Ingot]{.index index="gamma" range="close"} here. Nothing outside this
chapter's own process pairs it, so a recovered pair indexes as though the
attribute were absent.

Which occurrence is the proper one, a role no other process resolved for a
recovered mark: [Jetty]{.index index="gamma" mention="principal"}.

An author's own id on a body mark, which recovery carries into the locator so
the index links to the passage rather than to the top of this page:
[Keystone]{#keystone-passage .index index="gamma"}.

A cross-reference mark carrying an author's id, which contributes no locator
however the chapter is read: [Lintel]{#lintel-passage .index index="gamma"
see="Escutcheon"}.

A range with an id on each end, which recovery prints as two locators because
nothing outside this chapter's own process pairs it: [Newel]{#newel-opens
.index index="gamma" range="open"} opens here and [Newel]{#newel-closes
.index index="gamma" range="close"} closes here.

A range with an id on the OPEN end only, so one of its two recovered locators
carries a fragment and the other does not: [Oriel]{#oriel-opens .index
index="gamma" range="open"} opens here and [Oriel]{.index index="gamma"
range="close"} closes here.

An author's id on a mark whose `mention=` role no other process resolved for a
recovered mark: [Purlin]{#purlin-passage .index index="gamma" mention="principal"}.

## A [Mullion]{#mullion-passage .index index="gamma"} in a heading

An id an author writes in a heading is relocated out of it on the render route,
so the page carries it below the heading; recovery reads it from the heading
where the author wrote it, and the two agree.
